description: Add or update up to 100 REAL contacts in one call (upsert by email) — the replacement for a CSV import. Contacts created here are real audience members: segments and campaigns include them, and each new one fires `contact.created` workflows. Only use addresses the user gave you; never invent or test with this tool (use volanea_track_event for test contacts). `tags` are added to every contact in the call as `data.tags` (existing tags are kept), so a campaign audience can be a segment on `data.tags` equals "<tag>". Safety: an address on the suppression list (hard bounce, complaint, unsubscribe, manual block) or an existing unsubscribed contact is SKIPPED untouched and listed in `skipped` — this tool never re-subscribes anyone.

company.description: Stored as the custom field data.company.

data.description: Other custom fields, e.g. { "first_line": "…" }. Available in templates as {{data.<field>}}. Field names: letters, digits, _ . -

project_id.description: Which project to act on — a projectId from volanea_list_projects. Optional when this connection reaches exactly one project; required when it reaches several (the call fails with the list of projects instead of guessing). A project API key only ever reaches its own project.

tags.description: Tags added to every contact in this call, e.g. ["outreach-nov17"]. Letters, digits, _ . - only.

name: volanea_upsert_contacts

code.description: Machine-readable failure code to branch on. Present only when success is false.

errors.description: Rows rejected as invalid: { index, email, error }.

segmentFilter.description: A volanea_create_segment condition matching the first tag, when tags were given.

skipped.description: Not written: { email, reason } — suppressed:<reason>, unsubscribed, or duplicate_in_batch.

warnings.description: Contacts written but still excluded from campaigns (created earlier as MCP test artifacts).

error.description: Human-readable failure reason. Present only when success is false.

success.description: False when the call failed; read `error` and `code` in that case.
